title: Quasi-finite saturation locus descends to the slice
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], and let $(U,R,s,t,e,i,c)$ be a groupoid scheme over $S$ [def-a1-groupoid-scheme], all structure morphisms being over $S$. Let $g:B\to U$ be a morphism of schemes. Assume $s,t,g$ are locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Put $H=B\times_{g,U,t}R$, $p=\operatorname{pr}_B:H\to B$ and $h=s\circ\operatorname{pr}_R:H\to U$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. There is an open subscheme $W\subseteq B$ [def-weil-open-immersion] such that $p^{-1}(W)$ equals the locus of points at which $h$ is quasi-finite [pqf-def-quasifinite], as open subschemes of $H$. In particular, $h|_{p^{-1}(W)}$ is locally quasi-finite, and if $h$ is quasi-finite at $(b,e(g(b)))$, then $b\in W$.

source.place: Tag 04LH (lemma-local-source), specialized by Tag 047W (remark-local-source-apply), item (2): P = locally quasi-finite, Q = R = locally of finite type.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-lft-base-change], the projection $H\to R$ is locally of finite type, being the base change of $g$ along $t$. Since $s$ is locally of finite type, clause (e) of [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] shows that $h$ is locally of finite type. By [lem-sc-quasi-finite-points-open], its pointwise quasi-finite locus is an open subscheme $D\subseteq H$, and $h|_D$ is locally quasi-finite.

source.place: Tag 04LH (lemma-local-source), proof, construction of W(P,h); Tag 047W (remark-local-source-apply), (2).

proof.text: Put $C=H\times_B H$, with projections $a,b:C\to H$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Write its universal components as $(\beta,r_1,r_2)$, with $g\beta=tr_1=tr_2$, and put $d=c(i(r_1),r_2):C\to R$ [def-a1-groupoid-scheme]. Then $td=ha$ and $sd=hb$. The map $(a,d):C\to H\times_{h,U,t}R$ has inverse $((\beta,r),v)\mapsto(\beta,r,c(r,v))$; the map $(b,d):C\to H\times_{h,U,s}R$ has inverse $((\beta,r),v)\mapsto(\beta,c(r,i(v)),r)$. These are scheme morphisms by the fibre-product universal property: $t(c(r,v))=tr$ and $t(c(r,i(v)))=tr$ give their defining constraints. Each inverse composite is the identity by associativity and the inverse and identity laws, for example $c(i(r),c(r,v))=v$ and $c(r,c(i(r),r_2))=r_2$. Thus the square with upper map $d$, lower map $h$, left map $a$ and right map $t$, and the square with upper map $d$, lower map $h$, left map $b$ and right map $s$, are cartesian.

source.place: Tag 03C6 (lemma-diagram-pull), explicit inverse formulas, pulled back along g; more-groupoids.tex Tag 04LH, second displayed diagram.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-scheme-quasifinite-at-base-change] to $h$ in each cartesian square of step 2. At every $z\in C$, $d$ is quasi-finite at $z$ if and only if $h$ is quasi-finite at $a(z)$, and also if and only if $h$ is quasi-finite at $b(z)$. Its hypothesis that $h$ be locally of finite type was proved in step 1; the base maps are respectively $t$ and $s$ and need no additional hypotheses. Consequently $a^{-1}(D)=b^{-1}(D)$ as subsets, hence as open subschemes [def-weil-open-immersion].

source.place: Tag 04LH (lemma-local-source), equality of the two inverse-image loci; morphisms.tex Tag 01TM (lemma-base-change-quasi-finite), (1).

proof.text: The identity law gives a section $\sigma:B\to H$, $\beta\mapsto(\beta,e(g\beta))$, of $p$ [def-a1-groupoid-scheme]. Define $W=\sigma^{-1}(D)$, an open in $B$. The pair $(\mathrm{id}_H,\sigma p)$ defines $j:H\to C$ by [def-pc-fibre-product], since $p\sigma p=p$. Pulling the equality of step 3 back along $j$ gives $D=j^{-1}a^{-1}D=j^{-1}b^{-1}D=(\sigma p)^{-1}D=p^{-1}W$. Equality of these opens is equality of their open subschemes by [def-weil-open-immersion].

source.place: Tag 04LH (lemma-local-source), final paragraph: the identity section and W = sigma^{-1}(W(P,h)).

proof.text: Since $p^{-1}W=D$, [lem-sc-quasi-finite-points-open] identifies $h|_{p^{-1}W}$ with the locally quasi-finite restriction $h|_D$ from step 1. Finally, if $h$ is quasi-finite at $(\beta,e(g\beta))=\sigma(\beta)$, then $\sigma(\beta)\in D$, so $\beta\in\sigma^{-1}D=W$ by its definition.

source.place: Tag 04LH (lemma-local-source), final sentence, specialized by Tag 047W (2); morphisms.tex Tag 01TI (lemma-quasi-finite-points-open).

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q146-28322f13c (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read the item in full, every cited statement, and the source: Stacks more-groupoids 04LH (lemma-local-source) with its proof and 047W(2) (P = locally quasi-finite, Q = R = locally of finite type, no flatness). The statement is unchanged from base and matches the source hypothesis by hypothesis; its conclusion p^{-1}W equal to the pointwise quasi-finite locus is W(P,h) by 01TI. There are no new nodes, no repair note and no SGA. Step 1: pr_R is the base change of g along t (lft-base-change), h = s∘pr_R is lft by clause (e) of the permanence node, and D is open with h|_D locally quasi-finite by lem-sc-quasi-finite-points-open. Step 2: I re-derived both inverse formulas with the groupoid laws of def-a1-groupoid-scheme (s∘c = s∘pr_1, t∘c = t∘pr_0). d = c(i r1, r2) is defined, t∘d = h∘a, s∘d = h∘b, and all four composites are the identity, so both squares are cartesian; this step is elementary. Step 3: lem-sfb-scheme-quasifinite-at-base-change applied to h (lft) along t and along s gives a^{-1}D = b^{-1}D. Step 4: sigma = (id, e∘g) and j = (id, sigma∘p) give D = p^{-1}(sigma^{-1}D), a clean replacement for Stacks' set-theoretic sentence. Step 5 is immediate. Edge cases checked: B empty, the identity groupoid (W is the quasi-finite locus of g), a trivial G_a action (W empty), a finite constant group (W = B), nonflat groupoids. No cycle. No duplicate: lem-sfb-relation-open-locus-descent needs flat lfp equivalence relations and g = id, lem-a1-groupoid-source-pullback-translation is a different isomorphism, and lem-sfb-space-quasifinite-locus-open is the algebraic-space version. The only citer, lem-sfb-cm-relation-point-slice, uses the item exactly as stated. I accept the declared tool use of lem-sc-quasi-finite-points-open (generic 01TI openness). The blueprint from.node det-thm-sf-ctf-stability-direct-images replaces the inherited null and is acceptable.

lean.statement: theorem groupoid_quasiFiniteLocus_descends {S U R B : Scheme.{u}} (s t : R ⟶ U) (e : U ⟶ R) (i : R ⟶ R) (c : pullback s t ⟶ R) (uS : U ⟶ S) (rS : R ⟶ S) (_hs : s ≫ uS = rS) (_ht : t ≫ uS = rS) (_he : e ≫ rS = uS) (_hi : i ≫ rS = rS) (_hc : c ≫ rS = pullback.fst s t ≫ rS) (hG : IsGroupoidScheme s t e i c) (g : B ⟶ U) [LocallyOfFiniteType s] [LocallyOfFiniteType t] [LocallyOfFiniteType g] : ∃ W : B.Opens, (∀ z : ↥(pullback g t : Scheme.{u}), z ∈ (pullback.fst g t ⁻¹ᵁ W) ↔ Scheme.Hom.IsQuasiFiniteAtPoint (pullback.snd g t ≫ s) z) ∧ Scheme.Hom.IsLocallyQuasiFinite ((pullback.fst g t ⁻¹ᵁ W).ι ≫ (pullback.snd g t ≫ s)) ∧ ∀ b : B, Scheme.Hom.IsQuasiFiniteAtPoint (pullback.snd g t ≫ s) ((pullback.lift (𝟙 B) (g ≫ e) (by simp only [Category.id_comp, Category.assoc, hG.identity_target, Category.comp_id])) b) → b ∈ W
